originalTitle: European Athletics Championships: Hudson-Smith claims 400m gold, Newnham takes 400m hurdles silver – as it happened
summary: Matt Hudson-Smith took his third European title in the men’s 400m while Emily Newnham stormed to silver in the women’s 400m hurdles
content: Stand … and deliver. On a balmy night in Birmingham, Matt Hudson-Smith powered past the stand bearing his name at the Alexander Stadium and into history by becoming the first man to win three European Championship 400m titles. And afterwards, as the adrenaline flooded his body and he posed wearing a crown in front of his own stand, the 31-year-old made it clear just how much it meant. “Nobody is going to beat me on this track,” he said. “This is my home. I have been here since I was nine. I know this track like the back of my hand. Great Britain 6 (3 gold, 3 silver) Italy 5 (2 gold, 2 silver, 1 bronze) Netherlands 5 (2 gold, 1 silver, 2 bronze) Norway 3 (2 gold, 1 bronze) Sean Ingle’s report is coming up – that’s the lot from me, see you tomorrow for more. “I was in the place I wanted to be, and unfortunately I was bashing arms with the guy next to me,” says Bennett. “Unfortunately that’s the name of the game … I’m happy to be here. “Not many people believed in me, for the last however long, so even being here is kind of defying the odds … on another day, maybe I’d have done it, but not today. “It’s not what I wanted, but I know I can be there … hopefully I get to prove it again soon.” A furiously fast finish and a time of 13.12sec for the Swiss sprinter. Just Kwaou-Mathey (France) second in 13.16sec, Szymanski (Poland) third in 13.26sec. Bennett of Great Britain seventh, in a time of 13.62sec. Last but not least: The men’s 110m hurdles final. Sam Bennett competes for Great Britain. Neugebauer of Germany leads the decathlon after day one, despite that disastrous run in the 400m heat. The analysts think it wasn’t cramp, just a serious excess of lactic acid. “The ‘lactic’ filled his body from head to toe there,” says pundit Jessica Ennis-Hill on the BBC. 1) Neugebauer 4483pts 2) Tesselaar 4412pts 3) Skotheim 4382pts 4 )Gletty 4323pts 5) Erm 4282pts Tesselaar wins that third men’s 400m heat with a PB, 47.06sec, then Dario Dester (Italy) and Nino Portmann (Switzerland): But Neugebauer endures a horrible finish, perhaps cramping up, and he almost crawls over the line as he finishes dead last! The third 400m heat in the men’s decathlon now coming up. Neugebauer of Germany is up now. Tesselaar of the Netherlands is there too. The 400m heats are ongoing, in the decathlon. And scheduled for 9.47pm BST is the men’s 110m hurdles final. After the women’s 400m, I couldn’t quite work out if Diallo of Portugal was weeping with sorrow having been beaten into third, or with delight at winning bronze … Now it becomes clear. Hearty congratulations to her. “I’m so, so happy. I knew I wanted a medal … I always think if I can focus on my processes, then who knows what can happen? I’m so, so happy,” says Newnham. “I knew being in lane nine, I had to go out hard, which I never seem to do … it wasn’t until I got to the bend that I could assess where I was at … “I work hard. The training times show that. But it doesn’t matter if you can’t put it out there on the track … I’m just so happy to do a performance that I think replicates that.” Emma Zapletalova (Slovakia) takes gold in 52.91sec, Emily Newnham with a PB of 53.33sec and wins silver for Great Britain, Fatoumata Diallo of Portugal bronze in 53.55sec. A dominant performance by Zapletalova who was expected to win gold. Wonderful stuff from Newnham, who powered past Diallo in the closing metres. Time for the women’s 400m hurdles final … Hudson-Smith has his gold medal. And a crown on his head. “Words can’t describe how much that meant to me … I was watching a BBC newscast, saying I was injured and everything. You lot need to come with the facts. “The whole point of rounds is to survive … The Dutch guy needed a PB to beat me. “We’ve got some big races coming up … it’s about conserving yourself … I knew I was the best in the world. “No one was going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I know this track like the back of my hand.” Fantini of Italy, the reigning champion, tries to deny Kosonen … but it wasn’t to be. Kosonen throws 76.28m to finish, and wins gold. Beatrice Llano (Norway) wins bronze. Back to the women’s hammer … “What I loved is when he came into the home straight,” says Colin Jackson on the BBC. “He took that deep breath and thought; ‘Right, let’s give it’.” Hudson-Smith is now situated in, well, the Hudson-Smith stand. Quite right too. That’s his third European gold medal. Muhammad Kounta takes silver in 44.40sec. Phijffers wins bronze in 44.41sec. Hudson-Smith was in the outside lane and took a healthy lead into the final straight. That lead was eroded as the finish line neared, but he did more than enough. Brilliant run. Sensational. The Briton wins in 44.17sec with world-class run. Jonas Phijffers is the man who beat Hudson-Smith in the semi-final. The men’s 400m final is imminent. All eyes on Matthew Hudson-Smith. “I wanted to put down just enough to make sure I got an auto-Q,” says Asher-Smith. “The important thing is to give every competitor the respect they deserve. “A ninth European medal is a carrot for the final … I sometimes don’t even know what number it is … I’m just trying to stay in the moment and execute.” Rhasidat Adeleke (Republic of Ireland) wins the third semi-final (22.43sec). Fabienne Hoenke (Switzerland) second. Success Eduan of Great Britain qualifies in third. Three British athletes in tomorrow’s final. “I felt really good,” says Eduan. “I knew this heat would be fast … I’m just so happy to have made the final … I’m gaining confidence, experience, This is not a full-time thing, I’m still juggling my degree at the same time. It’s not an opportunity I’m going to take for granted.” “I would give that a good eight, solid eight,” Hunt tells the BBC. “My plan was to put down a really, really hard turn, kill them to 150, and no one was ever going to hang with me … I think that’s my second-quickest time this year, [I was] chilling at the end, so – exciting … see you in the final.” Hunts wins in 22.38sec. chineseTitle: 欧洲田径锦标赛：哈德森-史密斯获得 400 米金牌，纽纳姆获得 400 米跨栏银牌——事实如此
chineseSummary: 马特·哈德森·史密斯 (Matt Hudson-Smith) 在男子 400 米跨栏比赛中第三次获得欧洲冠军，艾米丽·纽纳姆 (Emily Newnham) 在女子 400 米跨栏比赛中夺得银牌
chineseContent: 站立……并交付。在伯明翰一个温暖的夜晚，马特·哈德森·史密斯 (Matt Hudson-Smith) 冲过亚历山大体育场以他名字命名的看台，成为第一位赢得三届欧洲锦标赛 400 米冠军的人，载入史册。随后，当肾上腺素涌入他的身体并在自己的展位前戴着王冠摆出姿势时，这位 31 岁的年轻人清楚地表明了这意味着什么。 “在这条赛道上没有人能打败我，”他说。 “这是我的家。我从九岁起就在这里。我对这条赛道了如指掌。英国 6（3 金，3 银）意大利 5（2 金，2 银，1 铜）荷兰 5（2 金，1 银，2 铜）挪威 3（2 金，1 铜）肖恩·英格尔的报告即将发布 - 这就是我的成绩，明天见更多。“我在我想去的地方，不幸的是我当时正在和旁边的那个人挥舞手臂，”贝内特说道。“不幸的是，这就是游戏的名称……我很高兴来到这里。 “无论过去多久，都没有多少人相信我，所以即使是在这里也有点不服输……改天，也许我会做到，但不是今天。这不是我想要的，但我知道我可以在那里……希望我很快就能再次证明这一点。”这位瑞士短跑运动员以 13.12 秒的速度完赛。 Kwaou-Mathey（法国）以13.16秒获得第二名，Szymanski（波兰）以13.26秒获得第三。英国选手贝内特排名第七，成绩为13.62秒。最后但并非最不重要的一点是：男子 110m 栏决赛。萨姆·贝内特代表英国队参赛。德国选手诺伊格鲍尔在第一天后就在十项全能比赛中领先，尽管他在 400 米高温中表现不佳。分析师认为这并不是抽筋，而是乳酸严重过量。 “‘乳酸’从头到脚充满了他的身体，”英国广播公司的专家杰西卡·恩尼斯-希尔说道。 1) 诺伊格鲍尔 448
